units.spine: The busiest way through the village runs into the market, so a traveller coming in needs no directions.
Armed company is kept here as a matter of course, at the charter hall and at the veteran's lodge.
In Hochhausen the arguments are about who stands where at the market, not about the price of bread.
The stone from the quarry and the boards from the sawmill go out past the parish bounds, and what the village cannot make comes in by the same road.
What the village could hold, it could hold for a short while and no longer.
The village would hold against the trouble it expects, though nobody here takes that for proof against the rest.
Nothing here is set against whatever lives beyond the fields, so each household answers for its own fences.
More quarrels are opened here than are ever settled.
Nothing in the village is spare, and it shows first in what is mended instead of replaced.
Nobody here works magic, no arrangement stands for calling in anyone who does, and neither is looked for.
Hochhausen eats out of its own fields, and a closed road troubles it less than a bad year does.
The Commercial Circle and the Administrative Circle are at odds quietly enough that people passing through meet the quarrel late rather than at the door.
Goods come into the village and go out of it at a pace nobody remarks on.
The road the village stands on is what it lives off, and a face nobody knows turns no heads at the market.
The village is the size a place of this kind settles at, no bigger and no smaller.
One of the ties this village keeps outweighs the others, and it is the one that decides what the place agrees to and what it refuses.
The people here are bound to one another by market day, the common grazing and the church, and by nothing else worth a name.
One gap shows in how this place is run, of the kind that one more body would close.
